headline: WFP cuts Gaza food assistance by one-third
dek: WFP will cut Gaza caseload from 1.6M to 1.1M people (about 500k lose monthly food/cash assistance); rations halved (1 parcel not 2); daily hot meals 250k->150k; cash assistance for 75k families cut from 1,250 to 750 shekels/month; West Bank caseload already halved in September (400k->200k). Needs…
sources: WFP (agency statement, country director Shaun Hughes to AFP, acting executive director Carl Skau to BBC/Reuters)
fault_line: Who pulled the plug on Gaza's food: Hamas aid diversion vs Israeli policy vs donor (incl. US) funding cuts?

sections.what_happened: WFP will cut Gaza caseload from 1.6M to 1.1M people (about 500k lose monthly food/cash assistance); rations halved (1 parcel not 2); daily hot meals 250k->150k; cash assistance for 75k families cut from 1,250 to 750 shekels/month; West Bank caseload already halved in September (400k->200k). Needs $450M for Gaza+West Bank through March 2027. WFP: 1.4M people (67%) face crisis-level food insecurity or worse; 200k in emergency conditions. UN teams recorded ~50 attacks/day in Gaza last week.
sections.what_verified: WFP's own statement + Hughes (AFP) + Skau (BBC/Reuters); AA, Dawn, Arab News, The National, UN News all carry same numbers.
sections.what_disputed: Israeli authorities maintain aid deliveries into Gaza are sufficient (bizwatchnigeria relay). Single-outlet claim (jowhar.com) that WFP cited Trump-era US funding cuts as a driver — not confirmed in WFP's own statement; treat as attributed report.
sections.why_matters: Humanitarian pocketbook: '500,000 people cut off on the eve of winter' — lead with the numbers (source-tagged), keep blame-framing as the debate question with all three sides represented.
sections.context: Background: WFP cuts Gaza food assistance by one-third: ~500,000 lose monthly aid, rations halved; needs $450M through March 2027
